messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV3 - Canary rollout for route `checkout-api` (canary=checkout-v2) is failing in eu-west-1. Automatic fallback to stable variant `checkout-v1` engaged, but we're seeing repeated sticky-affinity rebinds and increased error rates for affected sessions. Paging oncall.

oncall_sre: seen this — errors spiked ~03:04 UTC, latency 5x for some EU customers. Investigating. @eng-runtime-lead can you triage model variant mismatch/fallback policy? :rotating_light:

eng-runtime-lead: joining. quick read: smart-routing decided canary was unhealthy -> routed to stable-v1, but session affinity TTL was short and reattachment is bouncing back to canary when capacity frees, causing a loop. early hypothesis: canary backend is oscillating between Ready/Overloaded.

emma_l: customer CS flagged two enterprise tenants seeing 20% 502s and session state lost. They're hitting the checkout flow. CS is already on a call with one customer (ID: ACME-42).

oncall_sre: logs from the router (snip):
```
2026-03-15T03:04:12Z router eu-west-1 route=checkout-api req_id=abc123 variant=checkout-v2 -> 502 upstream: overload
2026-03-15T03:04:13Z router eu-west-1 req_id=abc124 fallback->checkout-v1 sticky_affinity=enabled ttl=60s
2026-03-15T03:04:13Z router eu-west-1 req_id=abc124 variant=checkout-v2 reassigned by health-check
```
Pattern: fallback then reassign within TTL window.

eng-runtime-lead: config snippet for the route's fallback policy:
```
route: checkout-api
  traffic: 10% canary checkout-v2
  fallback_policy:
    mode: sticky
    ttl_seconds: 60
    on_failure: fallback-to-stable
```
We may need to temporarily set `mode: stateless` or increase TTL to avoid mid-session rebinds until canary stabilizes.

sanjay_p: quick mitigation options I can run now:
- pause rollout to freeze traffic at current distribution
- increase sticky TTL to 5m
- set fallback mode to stateless (no rebind) so once a session falls back it stays on stable for TTL
Which one do we want? oneshot change preferred for quick restore.

oncall_sre: pause rollout first. Then change TTL. Pause command:
```
# pause canary rollout
redwood rollout pause --route checkout-api --canary checkout-v2 --reason "auto-pager: canary oscillation"
```
I can run that now.

eng-runtime-lead: good. Also add a temporary override to prefer stable for new sessions from eu-west-1 until we root-cause.

oncall_sre: running pause now... done. Verified traffic distribution stabilized at 0% new canary traffic in eu-west-1. :white_check_mark:

ops_bot: deploy-bot: rollout pause for checkout-api by oncall_sre at 2026-03-15T03:07:10Z — status: success.

emma_l: notifying the two affected enterprise customers that we've paused the canary and are mitigating; CS call updated. ETA for full recovery 10-20m, will update.

eng-runtime-lead: next step: increase sticky TTL to 300s and set fallback mode to stateless for region eu-west-1. Command to apply override (non-disruptive):
```
redwood config apply --route checkout-api --region eu-west-1 --set "fallback_policy.mode=stateless,fallback_policy.ttl_seconds=300"
```

oncall_sre: applying override... done. Verified via API that routes for eu-west-1 now have stateless fallback and TTL=300.

oncall_sre: monitoring: error rate dropped from 18% -> 2% over last 2 minutes, p95 latency back to baseline for most traffic. Continuing to watch for any residual stateful rebinds.

cs_lead: ACME-42 on hold, appreciate quick action. They'll want postmortem and timeline. I'll collect affected sessions and start impact summary.

eng-runtime-lead: root cause followup: initial failure appears to be a resource pressure on canary pods caused by a code path change combined with lower capacity in eu-west-1 overnight autoscaler bug. Canary health probe recovered intermittently causing flip-flop. Action items:
- rollback canary patch and redeploy after fix
- investigate autoscaler race
- adjust canary policy defaults: prefer stateless fallback when canary traffic < 20% and region infra unstable

sanjay_p: will open follow-up ticket and assign to eng-runtime, infra-autoscaler teams. Tagging: @eng-runtime-lead, @infra-oncall.

oncall_sre: handoff: I'm going offline in 10m. @eng-runtime-lead taking ownership for postmortem and customer comms. If anything spikes, escalate to SEV2.

eng-runtime-lead: ack — taking over. I'll coordinate the rollback and postmortem. Thanks everyone. :v:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated (canary paused + fallback mode changed). Severity downgraded to SEV4. Monitor for 60m then close if stable.

oncall_sre: last check — no new 5xx alerts in eu-west-1 for 5m. Marking this thread as stabilized. Will add logs and timeline to ticket.

cs_lead: leaving note for customers: action taken, ETA for permanent fix 48h, will send follow-up communication.

eng-runtime-lead: opened PM-4823 with timeline and next steps. Will add a short RCA and include config diff. Closing handoff.
